text:
erin: heads-up — hit a reproducible hang in the Go generator sample when cancelling mid-handshake during token refresh. tiny repro in the gist: https://internal.gists/redwood/go-gen-cancel-repro
miguel: thanks. what's the visible symptom?
erin: caller cancels context, function returns, but goroutines remain. stacks point to stream.reader waiting on authCh recv and refresher blocked on authCh send.
joan: sounds like a blocked channel send with no select on ctx.Done(). refresher should avoid blocking indefinitely.
erin: exact stack snippets:
  goroutine 91 [chan receive]:
    github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go/stream.(*reader).loop
    /repo/sdk-go/stream/reader.go:84 +0x...
  goroutine 92 [chan send]:
    github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go/auth.(*refresher).notify
    /repo/sdk-go/auth/refresher.go:50 +0x...
miguel: quick fix: when refresher notifies, do a select { case authCh <- tok: case <-ctx.Done(): return } so it doesn't block.
erin: I tried that and it eliminated the leak in the harness, but it highlighted a UX gap: our public API Subscribe(ctx) returns a channel and the library owns goroutines, so cancellation semantics are ambiguous. callers often forget to Close or assume ctx cancel is enough.
joan: proposal: introduce a pull-style API: Pull(ctx, req) (Stream, error) where Stream has Recv(ctx) (Chunk, error) and Close() methods. That makes ownership explicit: Recv observes caller ctx, Close releases resources.
miguel: that aligns with common Go patterns (io.Reader-ish). we can keep Subscribe for compatibility by implementing it as a lightweight shim that forwards Recv->chan and closes correctly. emit a deprecation log when used.
erin: added TestCancelDuringHandshake in stream/stream_test.go that simulates delayed refresh. master shows ~3 goroutines leaked per cancel; branch with select-on-ctx + Pull/Recv shows no leaks. CI: https://ci.internal/streams/3819 (failing on master).
ci-bot: build 3819 failed: TestCancelDuringHandshake reproducer attached in PR #4890.
docs-bot: please add migration docs in docs/sdk/go/streaming.md and an example under sdk/go/examples/generator-pull demonstrating defer stream.Close() and Recv(ctx) loop. Also note parity differences: Python/TS close net.Conn which unwinds goroutines; Go will prefer explicit Close/Recv and needs a migration note for Dedicated customers.
joan: UX suggestion: example should show context timeout + defer cancel(), then immediately defer stream.Close() so newbies don't forget. add a comment: // don't forget to Close() to avoid leaked goroutines.
miguel: perf check: Recv(ctx) adds a context check per call; add BenchmarkStreamRecv in stream/bench_test.go to ensure no perceptible overhead at typical QPS. if needed, optimize by reusing contexts or minimizing allocations.
erin: I'll open an RFC describing the v2 pull-style API, include migration shim, unit tests, examples, and changelog entry. tagging @miguel @joan for review. thanks!
